clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A nurse manager is helping update the hospital's OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Exposure Control Plan. Which statement about the required exposure determination is correct?

options.A: It identifies exposed job classifications and tasks without considering whether staff usually wear PPE.
options.B: It includes only staff who have already experienced a needlestick or splash exposure.
options.C: It excludes tasks performed with gloves because PPE removes the occupational-exposure classification.
options.D: It is limited to operating-room and laboratory staff rather than other exposed job classifications.

semantic_correction.rationale: OSHA requires employers with occupationally exposed employees to maintain a written Exposure Control Plan that includes an exposure determination. The determination identifies job classifications in which all or some employees have occupational exposure and, when only some employees in a classification are exposed, the tasks and procedures in which exposure occurs. OSHA explicitly states that this determination is made without regard to the use of personal protective equipment. Therefore, routine PPE use does not remove an otherwise reasonably anticipated occupational exposure from the determination.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Recognize that OSHA bloodborne-pathogen exposure determination is based on reasonably anticipated occupational exposure by job classification and task, without regard to PPE use.
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Current federal OSHA standard accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(1)(i)–(ii); 1910.1030(c)(2)(i)(A)–(C); 1910.1030(c)(2)(ii) — exposure determination made without regard to PPE
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: The Exposure Control Plan must include an exposure determination identifying exposed job classifications and tasks/procedures, and OSHA requires that determination to be made without regard to personal protective equipment.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: narrowed the item to OSHA's distinctive exposure-determination rule, removed the uniquely long correct answer and absolute distractor, and rebuilt all options as parallel statements about who/tasks are included in the exposure determination.

audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed pp. 24 and 26
audit_findings_append.finding: The original item tested a broad list of plan components and had a conspicuously long answer. The revised item tests one exact OSHA rule: exposure determination is based on job/task exposure without regard to PPE.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches OSHA's required job/task exposure determination and the explicit instruction to disregard PPE when classifying exposure.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Occupational exposure is reasonably anticipated exposure from job duties; a prior exposure incident is not required.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. OSHA expressly says exposure determination is made without regard to PPE use.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. OSHA requires consideration of all relevant job classifications and tasks, not only operating-room or laboratory roles.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone reflects both the required scope of the exposure determination and OSHA's explicit without-regard-to-PPE rule.
cueing_check: All four choices are statements about exposure-determination scope and are comparable in length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
